clue.text: Thus take advantage of capturing pawn, resulting in mate

indicators.note: in chess a piece that captures takes another into its keeping, so one string here takes a letter inside it

blocks.note: thus, in this way
to use someone is to take advantage of them
P is the chess notation for a pawn

explanation.surface: A chess move: grabbing a pawn and so leading to checkmate.
explanation.walkthrough: The first two pieces make one word that takes the pawn inside after its first letter. 'Mate' looks like checkmate but is a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate in the sense of a life partner is a husband or wife.

clue.text: Stupidly sue prior or head of monastery

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it in a muddled way, so these letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly takes legal action against a monastic official or the abbot himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A superior is the person in charge of a religious house, such as a Mother Superior or a Father Superior.

clue.text: It's inside cover, though not hidden

indicators.note: the answer is said to sit inside the words that follow, tucked across their join

blocks.note: letters running from the second letter of the first word into the next

explanation.surface: Something is tucked inside a cover yet somehow not concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is concealed in the clue while itself meaning 'not hidden'; ignore the comma, which punctuation never blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly visible, the opposite of concealed.

clue.text: Notices needing to be reorganized, in part

indicators.note: reorganizing means putting things into a new arrangement, so these letters change order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Some notice boards need partly tidying up.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a part or division of a whole.

clue.text: Lists characters in period pieces

blocks.note: first meaning: names the letters of a word in order
second meaning: stretches or pieces of time, as in a spell of work

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a theatre programme listing the cast of costume dramas; 'characters' are letters and 'period pieces' are bits of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a word is to give its letters in turn, and spells are short periods of time.

clue.text: Incomplete painting, one framed by friend

indicators.note: a picture framed by something is surrounded by it, so these letters sit within another word

blocks.note: a pal is a friend
painting is a form of art
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An unfinished painting has been put in a frame by a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means only in part, so not complete.

clue.text: Sea-monster left a haven it disturbed

indicators.note: things disturbed are knocked out of their settled positions, so these letters move around

blocks.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A sea-monster has stirred up a safe harbour and then departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'it' is part of the anagram letters, not a pointer back to the monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Leviathan is the huge sea creature of the Bible, used generally for any sea-monster.

clue.text: Be visibly pleased about current device, comparatively speaking

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps itself around a letter

blocks.note: smiling shows pleasure on the face
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone smiles at an electrical gadget, which counts as a modest compliment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively speaking' belongs to the definition: a figure of speech that works by comparison.
explanation.definitionFit: A simile is a literary device comparing one thing to another using like or as.

clue.text: Stimulant reduced — that's a blow

blocks.note: an upper is slang for a stimulant drug
cut means reduced, as in cut prices

explanation.surface: Being given a weaker dose of stimulant comes as a disappointment.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch thrown upwards, as in boxing, so it is a kind of blow.

clue.text: Extinct reptile as inspiration for poetry in bizarre script

indicators.note: something bizarre is strange and out of the normal order, so these letters get scrambled
in here means placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dinosaur becomes the subject of verse written in a strange hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The Muses were said to inspire the arts; Erato was the one for poetry. She goes inside the jumbled SCRIPT.
explanation.definitionFit: Triceratops was a three-horned dinosaur, a reptile that died out millions of years ago.

clue.text: Minister and a politician get in better shape

blocks.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a minister of religion
taken as written
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A cabinet minister and a backbencher go to the gym together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' points at government, but here it is a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To revamp something is to renovate or improve it, putting it in better condition.

clue.text: Something funny about king in court paper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the other letter

blocks.note: wit is a clever remark that amuses
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A royal court circulates a comic document about the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written order issued by a court of law.

clue.text: I, with car, returned piece of furniture not matched by others

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read from end to start

blocks.note: taken as written
the Mini is a classic small British car
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone got their car back and an unrivalled bit of furniture too.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car made since 1959; only the car is turned round, not the furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimitable means impossible to copy, so unique and unequalled by anyone else.

clue.text: Widespread affluence in Australia, for example

blocks.note: common means found everywhere
wealth is affluence, riches

explanation.surface: Prosperity is spread broadly across a country such as Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' marks Australia as one instance of the answer, not a place in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia's official name is the Commonwealth of Australia, and it belongs to the Commonwealth of Nations.

clue.text: Put in mouth after short time, consume inferior cheese

indicators.note: put in after tells us where to place one piece, namely at the end of the others

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a short time
to use up is to consume
trap is slang for mouth, as in shut your trap

explanation.surface: An order to pop something into the mouth briefly and eat some poor-quality cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is read as: put the word for mouth after the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is British slang for cheap, unappetising cheese, the kind used to bait a trap.

clue.text: From food store, extremely useful service for the housebound

blocks.note: a deli, or delicatessen, sells prepared food
very means extremely

explanation.surface: A food shop offers a very helpful service to people who cannot leave home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely useful' looks like one phrase, but 'extremely' does the wordplay while 'useful' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Home delivery brings goods to the door, which helps those unable to go out.

clue.text: Lines European put in not edited and not disputed

indicators.note: items put in something are placed inside it, so these letters go within another word

blocks.note: text that has not been edited is unaltered
L is short for line, doubled for lines
E is short for European

explanation.surface: A European inserts some lines into a text that is otherwise untouched and accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: The two short pieces join first, then go inside the word for unedited.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchallenged means not questioned or contested by anyone.

clue.text: Endlessly hear everything, and express disapproval

indicators.note: without its end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it
all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone listens to everything without pause and then complains.
explanation.definitionFit: To catcall is to whistle or jeer to show disapproval, typically at a performer.

clue.text: Rum diluted for protesting worker

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange, so these letters end up in an odd order

blocks.note: taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Watered-down rum is handed out to a worker on strike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink being diluted, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were English textile workers who protested against machinery by smashing it.

clue.text: Gently stroke husband, so upset it arouses pity

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means tipped over, so the short word is turned upside down

blocks.note: to pat is to tap or stroke lightly
H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wife soothes her distraught husband with a gentle pat, a touching sight.
explanation.walkthrough: SO turned up becomes OS at the bottom of this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in writing or a situation that evokes sympathy and sadness.

clue.text: Father tore part of coat — it's a state he's in

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
rent is an old past tense of rend, to tear
a hood is a part of some coats

explanation.surface: Dad has ripped his coat and is clearly in a state about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' in the definition refers back to the father: being a father is a state he is in.
explanation.definitionFit: Parenthood is the condition of being a parent, which a father is.

clue.text: Alternative to apple, we hear, for Adam and Eve, say

indicators.note: what we hear is a word picked up by ear, so it is spelt differently from how it is said

blocks.note: a pear is another fruit, an alternative to an apple

explanation.surface: A different fruit might have tempted Adam and Eve in Eden.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple suggests the forbidden fruit of Eden, nicely tying the two halves of the clue together.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve are the original couple, two people forming a pair.

clue.text: Penny and others making bit of a bloomer

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny
et al is Latin shorthand for and others

explanation.surface: Penny and her friends make a small mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a blunder, but here it is something that blooms, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one part of a flower, a thing in bloom.

clue.text: Highly competent guide retraces her path, but not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the answer lies within them

blocks.note: letters running across the ends of the words

explanation.surface: A skilled guide goes back along the route she came, but stops short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retraces' suggests reading backwards, but the answer runs forwards from the end of that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are Himalayan people famed as expert mountain guides, highly competent at altitude.

clue.text: What'll turn us into superpower?

blocks.note: surface reading: what might make our nation into a world-dominating power
setter's reading: what turns the lower-case letters 'us' into the capitalised name of the American superpower

explanation.walkthrough: The 'superpower' is the United States, written US. Typing those letters with a keyboard key held down makes them capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: On a keyboard, holding this key produces capital letters, changing us to US.

clue.text: Provide in flexible way

blocks.note: first meaning: to furnish or give
second meaning: the adverb from supple, pronounced differently

explanation.walkthrough: The two meanings are spelt alike but said differently: one rhymes with 'apply', the other with 'simply'.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply is to provide, and supply also serves as the adverb of supple, meaning pliantly.

clue.text: Again show power in a kind of race

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so one letter sits within another word

blocks.note: a relay is a race run by teams in stages
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A broadcaster reruns the power-boosted leg of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is showing a recording again, so to replay is to screen once more.
